title: Faster first page load: one-lock hydrate from the connect packet, diffed against compiled defaults
author: FarhanAliRaza

recent_comments.excerpt: Confidence Score: 5/5. The atomic Redis script checks ownership and writes the state tree as one server-side operation; malformed hash lists now reliably fall back to a full snapshot.
Codex Review Summary -- Code Review completed on commit 2d9abce.

notes: Largest and most invasive of the batch: combines hydrate+on_load into one connect-packet event, diffs first hydrate against compiled defaults (only sends vars that differ), and replaces the redis state-tree save with one lock-checked Lua script. 19 files changed across reflex, reflex-base and packages/reflex-components-core equivalents (compiler templates, event processor, app.py, redis manager). Author claims hydrate payload 36.5KB -> 2.1KB and redis commands per first load 291 -> 55 on a 20-substate benchmark app.

Very active single-session review/fix loop: 17 review threads opened by greptile/cubic/codex across 5 head-commits between 20:45 and 21:33Z, every one addressed and marked resolved by the author in the same window (0 unresolved). Includes a real cubic P0 that was investigated and rebutted with evidence rather than blindly accepted (CompileVars.CONNECT_AUTH_EVENT genuinely exists in reflex-base, not reflex, per commit e923225) -- worth a human double-check given the severity label, even though the author's rebuttal cites a passing unit test and CI is fully green.

All 111 checks green, including the full integration-app-harness/playwright matrix across memory/redis state managers and Python 3.10-3.14 -- unusually thorough coverage for same-day review, but still zero human (non-author) review to date.

Self-authored MEMBER PR; last_maintainer_activity_at is null (no MEMBER besides the author has commented), so days_waiting_on_maintainer (0.8d) is time since the author's last push, not a maintainer going quiet. Given the size and protocol-level change (frontend/backend boot handshake), this is the PR in the batch most in need of an actual maintainer read before merge, not just green CI.
Part of the ~15-PR Alek99/FarhanAliRaza Sep 5-7 performance push. No direct file overlap checked against sibling PRs beyond noting the shared authorship and theme.
